study_material.title: Functions - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: A function maps each input to exactly one output. Placement questions test evaluation, composition (f of g), inverses, domain/range, and even-odd symmetry - all mechanical once the definitions are second nature.
learning_objectives: Find domains and ranges of simple functions

concepts.heading: 1. Definition and Evaluation
concepts.body: f(x) = 2x + 3 means: whatever goes in, double it and add 3. f(4) = 11. Domain = allowed inputs; Range = achieved outputs. A mapping is a function only if every input has exactly one output.

concepts.heading: 2. Composition
concepts.body: (f o g)(x) = f(g(x)) - apply g first, then f. Order matters: with f(x) = x^2 and g(x) = x + 1, f(g(2)) = f(3) = 9 but g(f(2)) = g(4) = 5.

concepts.heading: 3. Inverse Functions
concepts.body: f^-1 undoes f. To find it: set y = f(x), solve for x in terms of y, swap letters. For f(x) = 3x - 2: y = 3x - 2 gives x = (y+2)/3, so f^-1(x) = (x+2)/3. Only one-to-one functions have inverses.

concepts.heading: 4. Domain Restrictions
concepts.body: Denominators cannot be zero: 1/(x-2) needs x != 2. Square roots need non-negative arguments: sqrt(x-3) needs x >= 3. Combine restrictions when both appear.

concepts.heading: 5. Even and Odd
concepts.body: Even: f(-x) = f(x), symmetric about the y-axis (x^2, cos x). Odd: f(-x) = -f(x), symmetric about the origin (x^3, sin x). Most functions are neither.

formulas: Inverse: swap x and y, solve
Domain excludes zero denominators and negative radicands
shortcut_methods: Evaluate composites from the inside out
Check even/odd by plugging in -x literally
For linear f(x) = ax + b, inverse = (x - b)/a
common_mistakes: Computing g(f(x)) when f(g(x)) is asked
Assuming every function has an inverse
study_material.summary: Master evaluation, inside-out composition, the swap-and-solve inverse recipe, and domain restrictions - that is the whole placement syllabus for functions.
quick_revision_notes: f o g means g first
Exclude division by zero and negative square roots

solved_examples.question: If f(x) = x^2 and g(x) = x + 1, find f(g(2)).
Find the inverse of f(x) = 3x - 2.
solved_examples.step_by_step: y = 3x - 2 gives x = (y + 2)/3; swap to get f^-1(x) = (x + 2)/3.
solved_examples.shortcut: Reverse the operations: add 2, divide by 3.

solved_examples.question: Which of the following is an odd function?
solved_examples.step_by_step: (-x)^3 = -x^3 = -f(x), satisfying the odd condition. The others satisfy f(-x) = f(x) (even).
solved_examples.shortcut: Odd powers of x are odd functions.
